I am old now, 81 years, and my hands are not strong like before. This small piece of land is mine, and I plant what my mother taught me — cassava with a few beans between them, the way we always do here in Kigoma. I have no money for the shop fertilizer, and I never used it; my parents never used it. I will put the goat droppings and the ash from my cooking fire on the soil, like always, and use the seed I kept from last harvest.
